raw.details:
Junior Robo Sumo – TechTrix'26

Event Details

  • Date: 23 October 2026

  • Time: 12:00 PM – 1:30 PM

  • Venue: Temple Ground, I.T.S Engineering College, Greater Noida

  • Registration Fee: ₹300 per team

  • Prize Pool: ₹8,000

  • Team Size: 2 participants per team

  • Coordinator: Mr. Krishan Raj Singh

Event Description

Step into the arena for Junior Robo Sumo at TechTrix'26! In this head-to-head robotics challenge, two teams go wheel-to-wheel in a sumo-style match, each piloting a custom-built, wirelessly controlled robot. The objective is simple: push your opponent's robot completely outside the competition ring while keeping your own robot in play.

Success depends on robot control, strategy, stability, and quick decision-making under pressure. Build your robot, master your controls, and prove your dominance in the arena!

Guidelines

1. Team & Robot Specifications

  • Team Size: 2 participants per team.

  • Maximum Dimensions: 350 × 350 mm (L × B).

  • Maximum Weight: 3 kg.

  • Maximum Voltage: 3S LiPo, 12.6 V (fully charged).

  • Control: Fully wireless, manual control only. Wired controllers and autonomous robots are strictly prohibited.

  • Power Source: The robot must carry its own onboard power source. External power during the match is not permitted.

  • Prohibited Systems: IC engines and compressors are strictly prohibited.

2. School Participation Policy

  • Multiple teams from the same school or institution are permitted to participate.

  • Teams from the same school may share and use the same robot (bot), provided it meets all technical specifications and passes the mandatory technical inspection.

  • If two teams representing the same school reach the Semi-Finals and are scheduled to compete against each other, the school must decide which one team will proceed to the next round.

  • The school's decision must be communicated to the Event Coordinators before the Semi-Final match. The selected team will advance, while the other team will be eliminated from the competition.

  • This rule applies only when teams from the same school are matched against each other in the Semi-Finals. All other matches will proceed according to the announced knockout format.

  • The Event Organizers' decision regarding the implementation of this policy shall be final.

3. Pre-Event Inspection

  • Teams must report to the arena at least 30 minutes before their scheduled match.

  • Every robot will undergo a mandatory technical inspection and weigh-in before competing.

  • Robots that fail to meet the prescribed dimension, weight, power, or control specifications will not be permitted to compete.

4. Arena & Match Format

  • Arena: A circular sumo ring approximately 1.5–2 metres in diameter.

  • Format: Single-elimination knockout, with byes assigned through a random draw if the number of participating teams is uneven.

  • Each match features one robot competing against one opposing robot.

  • A robot is considered out the moment any part of it touches the floor outside the competition ring.

  • Each match lasts a maximum of 5 minutes.

  • If a robot loses power or completely stops functioning during the match, it will be disqualified from that match, and the opponent will advance.

  • The referee may stop a match for safety concerns, technical issues, or other circumstances requiring intervention.

5. Judging Criteria

If neither robot is eliminated within the 5-minute time limit, the referee will determine the winner based on the following criteria:

  • Aggression: Which robot consistently initiates attacks and attempts to push the opponent out of the ring.

  • Strategy: The effectiveness of the tactics used to push the opponent or avoid being pushed out.

  • Control: Which robot demonstrates better control of its movements, positioning, and stability.

The referee's assessment of these criteria will determine the winner if the match cannot be decided through elimination.

6. Disqualification

The following will result in immediate disqualification:

  • Using fire or flame-based systems.

  • Using projectile-launching systems.

  • Using chemical or corrosive substances.

  • Using RF interference or signal-disruption devices.

  • Using any mechanism specifically designed to injure a person.

  • Exceeding the published dimension, weight, or voltage limits.

  • Using a wired controller or autonomous operation.

  • Receiving unauthorized external assistance during a match.

  • Poor social conduct, misbehaviour, foul or abusive language, or unsportsmanlike conduct.

  • Intentionally damaging the competition ring, campus property, or another team's robot.

7. Authority & Final Decisions

The Event Jury, Referee, and Technical Committee hold final authority over match outcomes, technical eligibility, disqualification, safety decisions, and rule interpretation.

Teams may present their concerns to the Event Coordinators. However, the organizers' final decision shall be binding.

Opportunities for Participants

Credential Sponsorship

  • Win credential sponsorship worth up to ₹15,00,000.

  • Receive event certificates through TruScholar's blockchain-powered digital credential platform.

Student Benefits

  • Lifetime access to the TruScholar Smart Credential Wallet.

  • AI-powered Career Coach.

  • AI-based Interview Preparation Tool.

  • TruResume – ATS-friendly AI Resume Builder.

  • Integrated Job & Internship Portal.

Important Note

Registration fees are non-refundable.

Build your bot, enter the ring, and push your way to victory!
